First, I should start by understanding what a prefill/decode cluster is. It's a part of the neural network processing pipeline where data is preprocessed and decoded. Disaggregated means the processing is split into separate components, which can be more efficient. Frontend pressure refers to high demand on the frontend, so the cluster needs to handle that efficiently.

Request routing is the process of directing requests to the appropriate parts of the cluster. Queueing would involve managing incoming requests, maybe using FIFO or priority queues. Tail latency is the time from when a request is received until it's processed. Cache transfer is about moving data between different layers of the cluster. Role switching might involve switching between different components or roles to handle different tasks. Batch completion is when multiple requests are processed in a batch, and GPU utilization is how much GPU resources are being used. Throughput tradeoffs are the balance between processing speed and resource usage.

I need to provide concrete examples. For instance, in a prefill/decode cluster, maybe the request routing uses a specific algorithm or queueing strategy. Queueing could be a priority queue with low latency. Tail latency might be measured in milliseconds. Cache transfer could involve data moving between layers with specific times. Role switching could involve switching between different GPU instances. Batch completion might be handled by a batch processing queue.
